lessons.description: Learn the essential morning greetings in Yoruba, focusing on the critical difference between addressing a parent respectfully with 'E' and greeting a sibling casually.

proverbs.text: Ilé la ti ń kọ́ ẹ̀ṣọ́ ròde.
proverbs.translation: Charity begins at home.
proverbs.contextNote: Literally meaning 'it is from home that we learn to adorn ourselves for the outside,' this proverb is used to emphasize that good manners—like greeting parents respectfully in the morning—are first established within the family.

proverbs.text: Ọmọdé tó mọ ọwọ́ wẹ̀ yóò bá àgbà jẹ.
proverbs.translation: A child who knows how to wash their hands will eat with elders.
proverbs.contextNote: Used to teach that a younger person who demonstrates good character and proper respect to elders, such as using the honorific 'Ẹ' when greeting, will earn their favor and privileges.
